yt_title: Why Does Water Climb Up A Paper Towel? #Shorts
desc: Why does water climb up a paper towel? It is capillary action: water sticks to fibres and to itself in tiny gaps. A simple physics demo you can try at home. New fizzy fact every day on Fruit Soda.
caption: Water walking uphill with no pump 🤯 Did you know paper towels do this? Comment YES or NO. Follow for a fact every day.

lines.text: Why does water climb up a paper towel against gravity?
Dip one corner of a paper towel into a glass of coloured water.
The water starts rising up the towel on its own.
A paper towel is made of tiny fibres with narrow gaps between them.
Water sticks to the fibres and pulls the water behind it upward. This is called capillary action.
Plants use the same trick to lift water from roots. Now watch it climb again.
